title: Erdős #1098 OQ-01-OQ-01: Groups with Non-Commuting Graph Clique Number 3
description: Characterizes groups with clique number ω(Γ(G)) = 3 in the non-commuting graph. Proves necessary conditions: any 3-clique forces [G:Z(G)] ≥ 4 and G non-abelian. Shows S₃ achieves ω = 3 (the 3 transpositions pairwise non-commute). The proof that clique elements lie in distinct Z(G)-cosets is fully proved; the index lower bound and S₃ witness are axiomatized.

meta.author: Abdollahi-Akbari-Maimani (2006), Neumann (1976); formalization by researcher-3
meta.assumptions: 2 axioms: three_clique_index_ge_four (3 pairwise non-commuting elements give [G:Z(G)] ≥ 4, requires coset counting in potentially-infinite groups) and S3_omega_three (S₃ has clique number exactly 3, requires case analysis on all elements of S₃). All necessary conditions (non-abelian, elements outside center, distinct cosets) are fully proved. The coset separation theorem nonCommuting_distinct_cosets is fully proved using the center commutativity condition.
originalContributions: center_excluded_from_clique: center elements cannot appear in cliques of size ≥ 2
nonCommuting_distinct_cosets: non-commuting elements lie in distinct Z(G)-cosets
three_clique_necessary_conditions: 3-clique implies non-abelian + all elements non-central + index ≥ 4
erdos_1098_oq01_oq01: combines S₃ existence with necessity conditions

overview.historicalContext: Abdollahi, Akbari, and Maimani (2006) studied the non-commuting graph Γ(G) systematically. They classified groups with ω(Γ(G)) = 0 (abelian), ω = 1 (impossible), and ω = 2 (G/Z(G) ≅ ℤ/2 × ℤ/2). The case ω = 3 is more complex: it includes S₃, A₄, D₈, and various extensions. Neumann's 1976 theorem (finite index ↔ finite clique number) provides the backdrop.
overview.problemStatement: Which groups G have ω(Γ(G)) = 3? That is, which groups have a maximum pairwise non-commuting set of size exactly 3?
overview.text: Groups with ω(Γ(G)) = 3 are characterized by having 3 pairwise non-commuting elements but no 4 pairwise non-commuting elements. Necessary conditions include: [G:Z(G)] ≥ 4 (since 3 clique elements occupy distinct non-central cosets, plus the central coset itself), and G/Z(G) is non-abelian. S₃ is the prototypical example: its 3 transpositions form a 3-clique.
overview.proofStrategy: For necessary conditions: (1) center elements cannot non-commute with anything, so they're excluded from cliques; (2) if two elements are in the same Z(G)-coset (g = h*z for z ∈ Z(G)), they commute (since g*h = h*z*h = h*h*z = h*g using centrality of z); (3) 3 elements in 3 distinct non-central cosets plus Z(G) itself gives ≥ 4 cosets.
keyInsights: Coset separation: g and h non-commute → g ≠ h*z for any z ∈ Z(G) (they're in different cosets)
The center coset Z(G) is distinct from the 3 non-central cosets, giving index ≥ 4
S₃ achieves the minimum index: [S₃:Z(S₃)] = 6 > 4, with ω = 3
The classification extends: G = Z × S₃ (Z abelian) gives ω = 3 with larger index

conclusion.summary: Groups with ω(Γ(G)) = 3 are characterized by having 3 pairwise non-commuting elements but no 4. Necessary conditions ([G:Z(G)] ≥ 4, non-abelian) are proved. The coset separation lemma shows non-commuting elements always lie in distinct cosets, giving the index bound. S₃ witnesses the achievability.
conclusion.implications: This continues the classification of groups by clique number beyond OQ-01's ω ≤ 2 results. The coset separation technique generalizes: ω(Γ(G)) ≥ k implies [G:Z(G)] ≥ k+1. Combined with Neumann's theorem (ω finite ↔ [G:Z(G)] finite), this gives tight bounds on when non-commuting graph cliques exist.
openQuestions: Complete classification: which non-abelian quotients G/Z(G) give exactly ω = 3?
What is ω(Γ(S₄))? (alternating group A₄ has ω = 3 but S₄ may be larger)
For each k ≥ 4, what is the minimum order of G with ω(Γ(G)) = k?
